div.head: Then the Book of Jeremiah the Prophet. and in It There Are 36 Chapters.
The Introduction.
div.ab:
In the thirteenth year of Josiah, Jeremiah began his prophesying. And after the complete captivity of Jerusalem, Nᵉvuzardån captain of the guard freed him in Ramah from the chains, that he might go where he wanted to. And since he lived in Jerusalem with the Jews who killed Gedaliah, he went down to Egypt; and there he was stoned. But the Egyptians, because they had loved him by whose prayer the crocodile animals disappeared, buried him on the edge of Pharaoh's palace. And when Alexander came to Alexandria, he took his body. But when the captain of the guard gave
him the Ark of Testimony, he hid it on the mountain in a cave, and it was never found again. And the fire of the sanctuary they threw in a pit; and seventy years after the return, when the temple was built and they organized the sacrifices, from the mud of the pit they sprinkled on the sacrifices and fire kindled - as Ezra shows. And Baruch wrote his book.

div.head: Section First.
div.ab:
(1:5)Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you, i.e. I chose you for prophecy. (1:10)See, I have given you authority today, i.e. the prophetic authority. (1:10)To root up, i.e. a type of the captivity; (1:10)and to build, i.e. a
type of the return. (1:11)A staff of almond I see, i.e. a type of the imminence, for (it) buds ahead of every tree. (1:13)A caldron set on I see, i.e. a type of Nebuchadnezzar. (2:7)But you<plu.> came and defiled with a of t and m my land. (2:10)Of the Kitheans with i of k. (2:13)Because my people have committed two crimes, i.e. one that (2:13)they forsook me, the spring of living water, and the other that (2:13)they went and dug themselves cisterns, broken cisterns that they can not hold water in, i.e. idols deprived of life. (2:14)Israel is not a slave, is he? i.e. he was a son but became enslaved to sin. (2:15)They roar with a of the second n. [Nestorian: with e of the first and quiescence of the second.] (2:16)Memphis and Tahpis, i.e. cities of Egypt. (2:16)They break you<f.> one by one, i.e. they take from you the poll-tax. (2:18)To drink the water of the Shihur, i.e. Shihur and Nile and Gihun - they are homonyms. (2:18)And the river Tigris, and by this typifying that though they take refuge in the Egyptian and the Assyrian they are not helped. (2:19)And your<f.> repentance will show you<m.> (to be) wrong with a of t, i.e. you are not truly repenting. (2:22)Nitre, i.e. borax. (2:22)Your<f.> sins have left scars in you, i.e. they have made a mark in you. (2:23)Can you<f.> say, I am not defiled? with a of t and e of ʾ.

div.head: Section Second.
div.ab:
(2:24)You<f.> snuffed the wind like a jackal, i.e. you roamed around like jackals.
(2:25)Keep your<f.> feet from running bare, i.e. do not spread out with desire for demons; and he calls stick and stone idols (in2:27). (2:28)For like the number of your towns are your gods, Judah. (2:31)I have not been a desert to Israel, have I? i.e. have I deprived them of goods? (2:32)A girl does not forget her ornament, does she? with å of d stopped, i.e. her charm. (2:33)Why do you<f.> lay your plans to seek love? i.e. how you have desired that I love you! but lo, your heart is with idols. (2:34)It was not by breaking in (that) I found them, i.e. not stealthily did they fear the idols, but openly. (2:36)Why do you<f.> think so lightly of repeating your ways? i.e. when she was subject to the Assyrian who was pleased with her and did not refuse (her), she dared a second time to take refuge in the Egyptian. (3:1)But you<f.> have played the harlot with many shepherds, i.e. you subjected yourself to demons. (3:11)The inhabitant of Israel has shown herself righteous, i.e. her sins are fewer than (those) of Judah, her faithless sister(3:11). (3:12)Go, proclaim [these] sayings [in the north], i.e. in Assyria in spirit, not in body. (3:15)And I will give you<plu.> shepherds after my (own) mind, i.e. Joshua the son of Juzådhåq and Zerubbabel. (3:16)In those days they will no longer speak of the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord, i.e. on account of the abundance of signs which will be, these first will be
disregarded.

div.head: Section Third.
div.ab:
(4:3)Light yourselves a lamp, i.e. understand
in your minds. (4:3)And do not sow on thorns, i.e. on idols, which cause harm without benefiting. (4:4)Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and remove the foreskin of your heart, i.e. cleanse yourselves. (4:7)A strong king is going up like a lion from his thicket, i.e. Nebuchadnezzar. (4:11)Like a straying wind, i.e. which blows in different directions. (4:12)A wind<or spirit> more full than these comes to me, i.e. the prophet speaks regarding his soul, which was filled by the Holy Spirit more than those in his days. (4:19)O my bowels, my bowels! I have pains and heart-aches! My heart beats wildly within me, and can not be still! i.e. he indicates by these the trials which are to come suddenly upon kings and commoners of the Hebrews from the Assyrian. (4:30)When you<f.> dress in scarlet, i.e. when you prepare yourself for fornication. (4:30)Your<f.> lovers have deserted you, i.e. your idols. (4:30)And they seek your<f.> life, i.e. your enemies. (5:8)Like lustful, wanton horses with quiescence of sh, i.e. stallions. (5:13)But the prophets will become a gust of wind, i.e. they are false.

div.head: Section Fourth.
div.ab:
(5:15)It is an ancient nation, i.e. the Babylonian, whose kingdom was old. (5:17)He will eat up your sons and your daughters, i.e. he will plunder. (5:27)A cage, i.e. a bird cage. (6:1)Beth-kᵉram is a large town of the sons of Benjamin.
(6:2)A fair and lovely one you<f.> are like with a of m. (6:3)Shepherds and their flocks, i.e. kings and their hosts. (6:4)Come on, let us go up at noon, i.e. the warlike men are speaking. (6:5)Let us go up against her at night, i.e. the crafty ones are speaking. (6:6)And all her oppression within her with quiescence of sh, i.e. her injustice. (6:10)Lo, their ears are uncircumcised, i.e. not giving heed to the truth. (6:15)They were not at all ashamed, nor did they know how to be restrained, i.e. by these words; in the sixth section (8:12) he repeats them yet again. (6:17)Watchmen, i.e. prophets, seers. (6:22)Is aroused, i.e. awakes. (6:23)Like the sea which rages with quiescence of k, i.e. which is tempest-tossed. (6:28)And like bronze and iron all of them are corrupt, i.e. corroding. (6:29)The bellows are lacking from their fire; and the lead, i.e. the word of prophecy has vanished on account of their rebellion, and they are not guarded from the fire by lead as silver (is). (6:29)And the refiner refines in vain, i.e. assays.

div.head: Section Fifth.
div.ab:
(7:14)I will do to this house..and to this town..as I did to Shiloh, i.e. it was deprived of the ark of the Lord in the days of Eli when the Philistines seized it. (7:18)To make cakes for the worship of heaven, i.e. hearts from wheat flour and honey and oil. (7:21)And they ate flesh, which I did not mention to their fathers, i.e. they sacrificed to demons. (7:29)The passing generation, i.e. which are going
into captivity. (8:1)They will bring out the bones of kings..and priests..and prophets, i.e. perhaps they would find gold in their graves. (8:6)I hearkened, i.e. I gave ear. (8:7)Their coming with a of m and ʿ.

div.head: Section Sixth.
div.ab:
(8:13)And I gave them, and they passed them by, i.e. they did not keep possession of the good things. (8:22)Is there no wax in Gilead? i.e. medicine in a mountain in which were many medicines. (8:22)Or is there no doctor there? i.e. by those of the body indicating those of the soul. (9:1)O that my head were water and my eyes springs of tears, i.e. would that! (9:4)For every brother is a sheer deceiver with stopping of the first k. (9:8)Laid in wait with quiescence of k. (9:21)For death came up to our windows and entered into our palaces, i.e. the Assyrian army. (9:26)And all with clipped beards, i.e. the Maʿadites, who trim their hairs. (9:26)For all the
nations are uncircumcised in their flesh, and all the household of Israel are uncircumcised in their heart, i.e. putting to shame those who glory in the flesh.

div.head: Section Seventh.
div.ab: (10:4)Nails, i.e. nails with a convex head. (10:13)He makes the noise of the rushing of water in the heavens, i.e. in the air. (10:17)Gather from the ground your<f.> shame, i.e. your idols. (11:15)And the flesh of the sanctuary they remove from you<f.>, i.e. your sacrifices stop. (11:16)To the sound of much split wood, i.e. a pile of faggots.

div.head: Section Eighth.
div.ab:
(11:19)Let us ruin
the wood with his food, i.e. as wood is ruined by food which is cooked, so let us ruin it by burning the body of the prophet.[But it seems to me that it was Let us ruin his food with wood, and the original writer made a mistake when to his food he added the letter b<=with>.] Greek: Come, let us cast wood, i.e. a deadly drug in his food which he will eat and die. (12:4)He does not see what becomes of us, i.e. our captivity. (12:5)Men on foot and a safe land, i.e. his cousins and their slaves. (12:5)Horses and flooding of the Jordan, i.e. the providence of our God; that is to say, if he keeps you from knowing your relatives, how shall you know the amazing deeds of God? God is saying to the prophet. (12:8)My inheritance has been to me like a lion in a forest, i.e. thus the Hebrews rebelled against me. (12:9)Has my inheritance become to me a speckled bird? Greek: has it not (become) a cave of a hyena? i.e. spotted by the worship of idols; mystically, the new church which is gathered from different nations. (12:9)With a bird circling it, i.e. the enemies. (13:1)Go, buy yourself a linen waistcloth, i.e. a type of the nation. (13:1)And gird it on your loins, i.e. a type of the providence which was over them when they went out from Egypt. (13:1)And do not dip it in water, i.e. a type of the crossing in the sea without getting wet.
(13:4)Go to the Euphrates and bury it there in a crack of the rock, i.e. a type of the exile of Babylon. (13:6)And after many days, i.e. a type of the seventy years of captivity. (13:6)And take from there the waistcloth, i.e. a type of the return. (13:7)And lo, it was spoiled and good for nothing, i.e. this is a type of the fact that though they return they will not prosper. (13:9)So will I spoil the proud ones <lag'ajå> of Judah, and the many proud ones <lag'ajå> of Jerusalem with a of l and ʾ after a g vowelless, since in the case of gaʾjå and paʾjå with a of g and p and consonantal pronunciation of ʾ you should pronounce gᵉʾajå and pᵉʾajå with quiescence of g and p and a of ʾ; as in the case of gavjå and pathjå: g̈ᵉvajå and pᵉthäjå. And because the Westerners are not accustomed ever to pronounce vowelless ʾ, they pronounce g̈aʾjeʾ and p̈aʾjeʾ with a of g and p and e of j, as in the case of hajå: hajeʾ. And it is manifest that the ʾ distinguishes gaʾjå and paʾjå from hajå. And the Qarqafensians say låʾgaʾjå, that is to say, after l with a they write ʾ and pronounce with a of g and å of j contrary to grammatical rule. And the Greek says Thus I am spoiling the shame of Judah and the great shame of Isreal.

div.head: Section Ninth.
div.ab:
(13:20)What is the flock which was given to you<f.>? i.e. that in the time of David there had been a thousand thousand, but lo, it was spent and brought to an end. (13:22)Your<f.> skirts are drawn aside and your extremities are revealed, i.e. you are exposed. (14:2)
And her cry with å of w and stopping of t, i.e. her grief. (14:6)They snuffed up the wind like jackals, i.e. she, being bereaved of her unfed offspring, nevertheless snuffs air alone until she dies. (14:16)Grave-digger with å. (14:17)The virgin
daughter of my people, i.e. that never yet has been ravaged. (15:1)Though Moses and Samuel stand before me, my soul is not pleased with this people, i.e. neither should you yourself be displeased that I do not comply with your prayer against them. (15:9)The mother of seven mourns, i.e. the Hebrew synagogue, which devised seven images for itself: the calf of the wilderness, and two calves which Jeroboam set up in Dan and in Bethel, and Manasseh's image with four faces. (15:9)Her belly is swelled up, i.e. with iniquities. (15:9)Her sun has set, i.e. her soul has departed. (15:11)I will not leave you in prosperity, i.e. (it is) to the people, not to the prophet, the Lord is speaking.

div.head: Section Tenth.
div.ab:
(15:17)Because thou hast filled me with anger, i.e. jealousy. (15:18)Have I been to me like treacherous water which is not reliable? i.e. because the anger delays, my words are not coming true. (15:19)If you return, I will restore you, i.e. from this way of thinking and do not doubt, I accept you. (16:16)Hunters, i.e. the Babylonians. (16:21)And they will know that The Lord is my our name, i.e. n signifying the trinity of substances
and l the unity of nature. (17:1)The sin of Judah is written with an iron pen and with a point of adamant, i.e. fixed, not to be erased. (17:6)In a salt land with å of m and a of l.

div.head: Section Eleventh.
div.ab: (17:11)Like a partridge which calls those that he has not born, i.e. the male of the <qeqbåne> partridges seizes the brood from females' nests and sits on them and produces young birds; but when they are grown they leave him and accompany their mothers. Thus are riches, which are gathered in iniquity. (17:12)A glorious throne, i.e. the kingdom of the promised land. (17:13)And rebels will be written down in the earth, i.e. they will be given over to the dust. (18:7)If suddenly I speak to the people, i.e. putting an end to the evil belief of those making destinies and casting fates. (17:16)The day of mankind <or the son of man> I have not desired, i.e. worldly desires. (18:14)The Mount of the Breasts, these are two twin mountains. (18:14)Or if (there) is withheld the cold, strange water that runs down, i.e. as water comes from afar and incontinently does not stand still that the sun may warm it, so the Assyrian is not restrained from them. (18:18)Come on, let us think up a scheme against Jeremiah, i.e. of murder, since he was exposing priests and scribes and prophets.

div.head: Section Twelfth.
div.ab:
(19:1)A jug, i.e. a bottle. (19:2)To the valley of Bar-Hånum, i.e. where were idols. (19:2)Of Hadhsith with a
of ḥ and l of s. (19:6)Tafath with a of t and p. (19:10)And you shall break it <tᵉbarjå>, and in other copies they write <tᵉburjå>. (20:1)Peshḥur with e of p. (20:1)Son of ʾAmarjå with a of ʾ and m. (20:7)Thou didst cajole me, Lord, and I was cajoled, i.e. I agreed to prophesy when thou saidst to me, (1:10)I have given you authority over nations and kingdoms and (1:19)They will struggle with you but not overcome you. (20:15)Curséd the man who announced to my father A baby boy is born to you, i.e. if he did not know that no man announced to his father, he was not giving way to cursing the non-offender. [(21:1)Mᵉlakja, Mᵉ asja with a of l and _].

div.head: Section Thirteenth.
div.ab:
(22:6)Gilead, you are the head of Lebanon, i.e. he thus addresses Jerusalem, who glorified herself; and he calls Jehoiakim Shålum(22:11). (22:14)And spacious chambers with a of r. (22:15)That you enjoy <methhadeʾ> cedars with d. (22:15)Your father ate and drank, i.e. Hezediah and Josiah moderately, but not like you - immoderately.
(22:19)With the burial of an ass he will be buried, i.e. they will drag him out. (22:23)You<f.> who dwell in Lebanon nestling in the cedars, i.e. deriding her. (22:30)Write <plu.> this man down proscribed childless, i.e. rejecting Jeconiah, who - though he had sons - yet was as if he had not, Zedekiah his uncle being king after him. (22:30)Because the man in his time will have no success with his poste
rity, i.e. showing that after his death the kingdom returns to his seed, for Zerubbabel was a grandson of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim.

div.head: Section Fourteenth.
div.ab: (23:5)And I will raise up for David a righteous shoot, i.e. literally Zerubbabel, but in a spiritual sense the Messiah. (23:6)And this is the name they will call him: The Lord Our Right with e of z, i.e. Our Portion. (23:9)A drunken man with quiescence of w. (23:10)And their course of life is evil, i.e. their activities. (23:18)For who has stood in the secret of the Lord? i.e. who of the false prophets. (23:23)Am I a God at hand with stopping of b and am I not a God far off? i.e. speaking reprovingly; however, God is near and far. (23:28)Why do you mix straw with the grain! i.e. true prophecies with false. (23:30)Who steal my words, i.e. conspire with each other to speak alike, (23:35)Thus shall you say, each to his neighbor, i.e. like prophets you shall consult each other.

div.head: Section Fifteenth.
div.ab: (24:1)Two baskets of figs, i.e. fruit baskets. (25:26)And the Arsacian king shall drink after them, i.e. the Babylonian, who was ruler over all of them. (25:28)And if they do not want to take the cup from your hand to drink, i.e. if they will not hearken to your words. (25:30)Hurrah, hurrah! i.e. this is a word of threat.

div.head: Section Sixteenth.
div.ab:
(26:2)Do not subtract even one word in the feminine gender. (26:22)ʾEljathån, son of
ʿAvakur. (27:2f)Make yourself a yoke and thongs, and put them on your neck and send them away, i.e. he did not command him to send the yoke and thongs to all those kings, only their types; and this is known from the fact that Hananiah the false prophet took them from his neck and broke (them) in sight of the people. And the son of Nebuchadnezzar is Mᵉrudhåkh, and his grandson Biltåshåsar (27:7).

div.head: Section Seventeenth.
div.ab: (27:9)Your <plu> dreamers, your diviners with å of ḥ and n. )27:19)Bases, i.e. bronze bulls which were under the flanks of the sea which was cast. (29:3)ʾElaʿså with e of ʾ and a of l. (29:3)Gᵉmarjå with quiescence of g and a of m.

div.head: Section Eighteenth.
div.ab: (29:17)Like bad figs in the feminine gender. (29:21)Qulijå with i of l, but some make it silent. (29:24)And Shᵉmaʿjå the Naḥmålite, i.e. who sees dreams. (30:6)Every man with his hands placed against his flanks, i.e. his sides. (30:9)And David their king whom I will raise up for them. i.e. Zerubbabel. (30:10)And he will refrain from war with stopping of k.

div.head: Section Nineteenth.
div.ab:
(30:23)Lo, the whirlwind of the Lord, i.e. the force of the Babylonian. (31:2)Found favor in the desert, i.e. the one who was led away in captivity instead of being killed in Jerusalem. (31:3)From afar the Lord appeared to me, i.e. he showed me something that was for the end. (31:15)A voice is heard in Ramah, i.e. this town is of the sons of Benjamin.
(31:15)Rachel weeping for her children, i.e. the mother of Benjamin, and by Benjamin referring mystically to all Hebrews as by part to whole; then the gospel (Mt 2:18) takes this in reference to Herod when it makes him the equal of the Babylonian. (31:22)For the Lord is creating a new thing on the earth, i.e.
another congregation. (31:22)The female woos the man, i.e. she leaves strangers and is restored to her master. (31:23)The Lord bless you, righteous abode, i.e. here the name for abode is taken in the masculine, but in all other places in the feminine gender, as in Abodes of peace are broken up. (31:29)In those days they will say no more, The fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children's teeth are set on edge with a of h and e of j, and in old manuscripts with å of q and j. [Greek: And the children's teeth are set on edge with a of ḥ.] (31:31f)And I will make with the household of Israel and with the household of Judah a new covenant, not like the covenant which I made with their fathers..when I brought them from Egypt, i.e. because at that time they did not abide in love for him more than three months, till they made themselves a calf; but after the return about three hundred and fifty years they continued in the worship of God, especially in the days of the Maccabeans. (31:39)To the hill of Gᵉråv with å of r.

div.head: Section Twentieth.
div.ab:
(32:9)And I bought the field from
Naḥmåʾjel, my uncle's son, i.e. by this he shows that Jerusalem would be restored. (32:11)And the document..sealed is a type of the keepers of the commandments, and which was not sealed is a type of the believers. (32:23)So all this misfortune befell them, i.e. it happened. (32:35)And their daughters to ʾAmelk with e of m.

div.head: Section Twenty-first.
div.ab: (33:13)From that time the flocks will pass under the hands of the one who counts, i.e. God commands the nation never again to get lost from him. (34:4f)You will not die by the sword, but you will die in peace, i.e. Zedekiah was not killed; but when the king of Babylon put out his eyes, he sent him down to Assyria; and he used to grind in the mill. And when he died, they threw his body out behind the city wall of Nineveh.

div.head: Section Twenty-second.
div.ab:
(34:18)The calf which they cut in two and passed between its parts, i.e. when they began to be troubled by Babylon, they set free the male and female slaves; and they set up a covenant that if they did not observe it they should be torn apart like the calf. (35:2)Go <plu.> up to the sons of Rᵉkhevjam with e of k fricative and a of j, i.e. descended from Junådhåv son of Råkhåv; and this to stand before me forever(35:19) indicates that they are priests from a tribe. And the Maccabeans too were from them. For when this man saw the people who were corrupted by sins, he renounced the world and its desires and went far away from man kind, and was living in tents like the ancient ancestors,
he and his sons after him.

div.head: Section Twenty-third.
div.ab: (36:4)Baruch son of Nirijå with å of b and i of n and r. (36:12)Dᵉlåjå with å of l and j. (36:23)Three or four columns, he cut it with a penknife, i.e. King Jehoiakim, who cut the roll with the penknife into three or four parts and threw it..into the fire. (36:25)The brazier, i.e. a copper brazier.

div.head: Section Twenty-fourth.
div.ab: (37:12)To divide the portion there with the people, i.e. the crop or wine of the land which he had bought from his uncle's son. (37:16)From the pit's rim into the pit, i.e. from the mouth of the pit they threw him down and did not let him down with a rope as usual. (38:7)ʿAvdamlek with a of ʿ and d, [and e of l]. (38:11)Worn out rubbing cloths with a of d and h, i.e. which had been (used for) wiping off horses after washing. (38:12)Your armpits with a of ḥ.

div.head: Section Twenty-fifth.
div.ab: (39:3)Nergel, Sheråṣår, Samgedh Nᵉvu, Sarsåkhim, Ravmågh, (39:13)Nᵉvushazbån. (40:5)And Nᵉvuzardån, commander of the guard, [i.e. the chief cook] gave him presents on the journey and let him go, i.e. not common things but the Ark of Testimony and the vessels of the worship. (40:8)Tᵉnaḥmath, ʿIfai, Nᵉtufath, Jazanjå; (40:9)Shåfån.

div.head: Section Twenty-sixth.
div.ab:
(40:14)Balʿis. (41:3)He slaughtered <paël>. (41:5)Their beards shaved...and agitated with fricative pronunciation of the latter t, i.e. upright
men were plucking their beards and were afflicted on account of what happened to Jerusalem. (41:8)We have storage pits in the fields with a of ḥ and stopping of d, i.e. pits of wheat. (41:17)Bemham.

div.head: Section Twenty-seventh.
div.ab: (43:9)In the mortar in the brick kiln, i.e. in the clay of un-dried brick. (43:13)The obelisk at Beth Shemesh, i.e. a temple of the sun. (44:1)Maghdul, Taḥpis, Memphis, Pathros.

div.head: Section Twenty-eighth.
div.ab: (44:19)The queen of heaven, i.e. Aphrodite. (44:28)Will prove true with e of n. (44:29)That you<f.plu> will know that my words prove true. (45:2)(This is) for you, Baruch,i.e. listen, Baruch. (45:4)Behold, what I have built I am tearing down, i.e. not carrying out the prosperity which I intended for the nation. (46:5)Are beaten. (46:6)They have stumbled. (46:11)Go to Gilead and get balms, i.e. this is a type that healing medicine did not remain for you<f.> in yourself.

div.head: Section Twenty-ninth.
div.ab:
[(46:16)The sword bringing low in the feminine gender.] (46:17)Pharaoh The Lame..- an agitator, but he lets the time slip by, i.e. by his own self he brings to nought his kingdom, through his picking a quarrel with the Babylonian. (46:20)Egypt is a pretty, spotted heifer, i.e. adorned with riches. (46:23)Cut down her forests, i.e. her nations. (46:25)ʾAmun of the water, i.e. Alexandria, which was built to the name of ʾAmun, an idol. (47:6)O sword of the Lord, how long will you<f.> not be still in the feminine gender. (48:9)Give
a crown to Moab, i.e. that she may set it on the head of Nebuchadnezzar. (48:9)her towns with å of j. (48:11)And settled on their lees with stopping of k, i.e. contented with their uncleanness. (48:13)And Moab will be ashamed of Kåmush, i.e. its idol. (48:17)The shoot, i.e. the root stock. (48:20)ʾArnun. (48:21)Måshur; Halun. (48:22)Jåhås; Mᵉfiʿath; Rivun; Nåvu; Devlatim. (48:23)Qurjatim; Gåmul; Mᵉʿun. (48:24)Qerjuth; Busår.

div.head: Section Thirtieth.
div.ab:
(48:26)Lay him low with d. (48:26)In his vomit. (48:28)The dove that nests on the ledge, i.e. on the ramparts. (48:32)Of Jaʿzir I weep for you<f.>. (48:34)ʾArᵉlå. (48:34)ʾEles, a heifer three years old, i.e. strong. (48:34)Namrim. (48:37)And their beards shaved, i.e. plucked. (48:45)Shåʾwån. (49:1)Malkum. (49:2)Rabath. (49:4)And you<f.> rely on your broad valleys, daughter dear, i.e. among your pleasures. (49:10)I have searched out Esau and have revealed his retreats. (49:12)Lo, those who were not obliged to drink the cup drank! i.e. the Hebrews, whose portion is the Lord. (49:19 or 50:44)ʾÅthån was a wise man, and by his wisdom his home was adorned. (49:14)And an envoy to the nations has been sent, i.e. the angel who assembled the Babylonians against the Idumeans. (49:20)The poor ones of the flock
will drag them off, i.e. the weak ones of the Babylonians.

div.head: Section Thirty-first.
div.ab:
(49:23)Råfådh. Sons of (49:28)Qedhår with e of q and the sons of the East(49:28), i.e. Arabians. (49:32)And their camels will be booty in the feminine. (49:35)Behold, I am breaking the bow of ʿIlam, the mainstay of their strength, i.e. all their fighting
was with the bow. (50:9)I am rousing, i.e. I am setting in motion. (50:21)Which I have commanded you<f.>.

div.head: Section Thirty-second.
div.ab: (50:39)Sirens will live in it. (50:39)Ostriches. And he calls Babylon the lodge of ʾÅthån (50:43) because of her opulence. (50:44)The poor ones of the flock, i.e. the Persians, who were weak at that time. (51:9)We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed; let us leave her...because her judgment reaches as far as heaven, i.e. her iniquity. (51:14)Alas, alas with å, and in ancient manuscripts pointed with e.

div.head: Section Thirty-third.
div.ab:
(51:25)Destroying mountain, i.e. Babylon. (51:25)And I will clear you off the rock, i.e. I will break your force. (51:27)ʾAradhat is the Qardu. (51:27)ʾArmen and ʾAshkᵉnåz, i.e. warriors joined with the Medes. (51:35)My despoiling, with a of z. (51:38)They bray, i.e. a bray is properly an ass's, but here it is stated about a lion in a borrowed sense. (51:41)How the Arsacian<f.> is caught; the praise of all the earth, i.e. Babylon. (51:46)When a rumor comes to her in this year, and after a year another rumor,
i.e. Darius plundered her in the first year, and in the second Cyrus seized her from him. [(52:1)Hamtul, the daughter of Jeremiah.]

div.head: Section Thirty-fourth.
div.ab: The Lamentations of Jeremiah. Some say [that before the captivity he spoke them in verse; but others say] after the captivity in Egypt when they took him with them by force. (1:1)The head of the cities, i.e. of Judah. (1:6)Her nobles are like stags, i.e. hunted. (1:11)They have set their desire upon provisions to restore life, i.e. they wanted bread to preserve life. (1:12)Not to all you passing along the way, i.e. sons of the world. (1:14)His yokes were bound to my neck, i.e. they were tied on.

div.head: Section Thirty-fifth.
div.ab:
(1:16)My children are exhausted, i.e. they are picked out of their time like unripe figs. (1:19)I called on my lovers, but they deceived me, i.e. upon my idols. (1:21)Bring the day which thou hast announced, i.e. which thou hast prepared for my enemies. (1:22)Many are my sighs, and my heart is miserable. (2:1)How the Lord in his anger has clouded over the daughter of Sion! i.e. made dark. (2:2)The dwelling of Jacob, i.e. [the land of promise. And (2:3)his horn, i.e. his strength. (2:3)And the flame has devoured his hands, i.e.] the work of his hands. (2:8)He laid down the measuring line, i.e. he measured her and delivered her to the Babylonian. (2:9)
Neither do her prophets experience a vision from the Lord, i.e. there remained with them no prophet at that time except him and Ezekiel. (2:21)Thou hast slaughtered and hast not pitied, i.e. like sheep. (3:3)Nevertheless he turns on me, i.e. he turns against me in his anger. (2:22)Whom I bore and reared. (3:4)My skin grew old. (3:5)He built against me, and a citadel surrounded me, and a desert. (3:16)And he has sprinkled me with ashes with å of p.

div.head: Section Thirty-sixth.
div.ab:
(3:27f)It is good for a man when he bears thy yoke in his youth; and sits alone and keeps silence, i.e. a type of the respected habit of celibacy. (3:29)He lays his mouth in the dust in order that there may be hope, i.e. he takes the vows. (3:33)For he does not afflict willingly, i.e. neglecting the discipline which they humbly adopt. (3:39)What does mortal man think? i.e. who is negligent and does not repent. (3:60)Their vengeance with e of n. (3:63)Their sitting down and their standing up I myself understood from their thought, i.e. he understood in the reverse way, as it were: From their sitting down and their standing up I understood their thought. (4:1)And the fine color fades, i.e. changes. (4:3)They<f.>uncovered their breasts like jackals and gave suck to their whelps, i.e. they are made naked like dumb animals; and it is said that jackals have paps in the breast like women. (4:7)Her Nazirites are whiter....than milk
with quiescence of d, i.e. their blood is sucked out. (4:7)They are red, they are singed. (4:8)Their skin has shrunk, i.e. it is dry. But the Babylonians who stripped them were not able to touch their garments. (4:17)Has sundered them, i.e. scattered. (4:20)The breath of our nostrils, the Lord's anointed, was captured in their pit, i.e. Zedekiah, who stood before us. (5:6)Gave a hand, i.e. had pity. (5:8)Slaves rule over us, i.e. of the Babylonians; for Nimrod, from whom the Babylonian kingdom originates, was not a son of Canaan who was called a slave but a son of Kush the son of Ham. (5:10)They have become shrivelled and ashen, i.e. by gloom. (5:13)Young men have ground with e of h the mill. And the first epistle of Baruch after the captivity was written in Jerusalem, and was sent to those taken captive in Babylon. And the second one was written in Babylon at the dictation of the captives, and was sent to Jerusalem before they fled to Egypt.
JEREMIAH ENDS.
